title: Cantilever, natural frequencies
description: Steel bar 200 x 20 x 20 mm, end x = 0 fixed. The square section bends the same way in y and z, so the first two modes share one frequency.

quantities.label: First bending frequency, mode 1
quantities.formula: (lambda1^2 / (2 pi)) sqrt(E I / (rho A L^4)), lambda1 = first root of cos(x) cosh(x) = -1 (1.8751)
quantities.citation: Timoshenko, Young & Weaver, Vibration Problems in Engineering, 4th ed., Wiley 1974, Section 5.3 (beta1 L = 1.8751)
quantities.tolerance_reason: Euler-Bernoulli theory ignores shear and rotary inertia, so 3D FEA comes out slightly lower (seen: -0.28 %).

quantities.label: First bending frequency, mode 2 (other direction)
quantities.formula: as mode 1 (square section: I is the same about y and z)
quantities.citation: Timoshenko, Young & Weaver, Vibration Problems in Engineering, 4th ed., Wiley 1974, Section 5.3 (beta1 L = 1.8751)
quantities.tolerance_reason: Euler-Bernoulli theory ignores shear and rotary inertia, so 3D FEA comes out slightly lower (seen: -0.28 %).
